title: Tale of the Bull and the Ass

keywords: tale of the bull and the ass
full_text:
In a fertile valley between the two great rivers lived a wealthy merchant endowed with a secret gift: he understood the speech of all beasts, birds, and creeping things. Yet this gift carried a strict warning—should he ever reveal to another human being what the creatures spoke, his peace of mind and very fortune would be forfeited.

In the merchant's courtyard stood a sturdy bull and a sleek, well-fed donkey. Each morning, the bull was harnessed to the heavy iron plow, driven through the rocky fields beneath the burning sun, and returned at dusk drenched in sweat and bruised by the yoke. The donkey, by contrast, spent his days resting beneath shaded palms, dining on sifted barley and clear fountain water, his only labor being to carry the master gently to market when occasion arose.

One evening, as the bull collapsed into the stable with weary groans, the donkey looked over with smug pity. "Friend," said the donkey, "why do you suffer so meekly? Tomorrow, when the plowman comes with your fodder, refuse to eat. Thrash the ground, moan as if struck by illness, and do not rise. If you pretend to be frail, the master will surely let you rest in the cool shade."

The bull thanked the donkey for his ingenious counsel. The next dawn, when the servant brought grain, the bull rolled his eyes, kicked his legs, and feigned dreadful weakness. The servant ran to the merchant in alarm. But the merchant, who had overheard the donkey's whispering the previous night, smiled knowingly. "Since the bull is too sick to plow," ordered the merchant, "harness the healthy donkey in his place and work him without mercy until sunset."

All through the scorching day, the pampered donkey was dragged through briars and mud, whipped whenever he faltered, and forced to turn the heavy earth. When dusk arrived, the donkey staggered back to the stall with broken knees, a bloody neck, and ribs trembling with agony. The bull looked up gratefully: "Blessings upon you, wise companion! Your advice brought me a day of sweet slumber."

The donkey coughed through dust and replied bitterly: "Hear my latest news, brother. As I labored, I overheard the merchant whisper to the butcher that if the bull does not stand strong tomorrow, he must be sold to the meat market." At once the bull leaped to his feet, devoured all his straw, and vowed to pull the plow with double vigor. The merchant, listening behind the partition, laughed heartily at how the meddlesome donkey had cured his own pride by tasting the bitter fruit of his own scheming.
moral: He who meddles unwisely in another's burden may find himself forced to carry it all on his own shoulders.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tale of the Bull and the Ass"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
